gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R2: '$42 per million input tokens, output free'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Wrong by 1000x. TypeSafe prices Jev at $42 per BILLION input tokens = $0.042 per million; output free.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R1: blog 'Introducing System One Models & Jev' dated 2026-01
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Page is dated Sep 15, 2026 (byline Diogo Almeida). R1's 'Diogo Almeida' and 'September 2026' elsewhere are right; the January date is wrong. R2's date and URL are correct.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R2: '100~200x faster than LLMs'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: TypeSafe's blog says 40x-200x faster (comparable intelligence, System One-shaped queries); homepage says 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper on its own four workflow evals and itself calls these 'the higher end of real world gains'. Independent runs found roughly 5x-25x (see systemonemodels.org digest, secondary).

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R1: architecture speculated as 'pointer-head'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: TypeSafe has not disclosed architecture; 'pointer head' is a feature of the third-party open reproduction Kev (per OrcaRouter), not of Jev. Press only says transformer-based and, per observers, perhaps built on an open-weight LLM.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: CHAT: Jev '4.69B' parameters (from an OrcaRouter blog)
gpt_discrepancies.finding: No TypeSafe statement of size; OrcaRouter pages I read say parameter count is undisclosed. '4.69B' not found.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: CHAT: latency 236-276 ms quoted elsewhere
gpt_discrepancies.finding: These are third-party p50s (AbdelStark pilot, nibzard DMB), reported second-hand by Laya/OrcaRouter, not TypeSafe's figure. TypeSafe's published range is 70-500 ms end to end; docs say about 100 ms for most queries.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: CHAT: 'Decision Index', 'decision-v7', 'JevBench' as benchmarks
gpt_discrepancies.finding: None is a TypeSafe benchmark. TypeSafe's own is Workflow evals (evals.typesafe.ai) and it publicly refuses a standard benchmark table. decision-v7 is Kev's training/eval suite; Decision Index and JevBench are independent community or third-party projects (several different 'JevBench's).

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R1/R2: training uses synthetic data (stated as fact)
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Not on any TypeSafe page I could read; comes from an Almeida interview reported by TechCrunch and repeated by Indian Express and Wikipedia.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Laya R2 ledger dates 2023-10 / 2023-11
gpt_discrepancies.finding: All Laya artifacts created Sept 2026 (GitHub 2026-09-18, HF 2026-09-18, receptron runtime 2026-09-19).

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Laya repo NandhaKishorM/laya (R1/CHAT) vs receptron/laya + convaiinnovations/laya (R2) is a conflict
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Both are real and not in conflict: NandhaKishorM/laya is the model author's Python repo (Apache-2.0, 34k stars, v0.4.13); receptron/laya is a separate org's Node/TS ONNX runtime (MIT, 985 stars); convaiinnovations is the HF org with weights (Apache-2.0). Whether NandhaKishorM is a Convai Innovations employee is not stated on the pages read.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Laya code MIT / weights Apache-2.0
gpt_discrepancies.finding: True only for the receptron runtime; the main Laya repo's code license is Apache-2.0.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Laya P50 about 32-33 ms on T4
gpt_discrepancies.finding: 32.8 ms is the multilingual checkpoint; English laya is 39.5 ms; 33 ms is the author's headline. Cloudflare's table lists 5.8 ms median for Laya with no hardware.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: fine-tuned 0.766 vs Jev 0.727 on typed-decisions
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Numbers match, but 0.766 is a fine-tuned checkpoint on that benchmark's split while base Laya scores 0.362; the Jev 0.727 is a third-party published figure.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: OrcaRouter: Laya 421M fine-tuned vs Jev '4.69B' zero-shot
gpt_discrepancies.finding: The 4.69B model is open RSI-Jev v6.1-VL (Qwen3.5-4B-Base), not TypeSafe's Jev; the article says neither project was benchmarked against the other. ECE 0.466->0.081 confirmed as calibration error after temperature refit.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Kev R2 ledger date 2024-08
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Kev repo created 2026-09-17; release kev-1.0 2026-10-01; HF kev-27b v2 2026-09-30.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Kev-27B within 1 point of Jev on unseen data
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Accuracy 0.851 dev vs Jev 0.857 supports 'within a point', but the Decision Index shows 52.3 vs 54.0 (1.7 points) and MMLU-Pro 0.675 vs 0.840; README says comparison is not controlled and the checkpoint was chosen after seeing test results.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Clef 'wins 3 of 4 Decision Index tasks vs Jev'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: The 3-of-4 is Typesafe workflow evals (invoice, customer service, security incidents; trails on agent trace), distinct from the 10-benchmark Decision Index where Clef beats Jev on 8 of 10 per blog.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: Perplexity pplx-decider-v1-27b priced $0.04 per million input tokens
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Perplexity docs list $0.02/M for pplx-decider-v1.2 (legacy IDs route to it) and $0.01 flash; $0.04 appears only on aggregator pages. Endpoint is /v1/decisions, no Jev wire-compat statement.
